mission:
Add two independent utilities to this library, each with unit tests:
1. In src/math.js add `clamp(value, min, max)` which returns value limited to the inclusive range and throws a RangeError when min > max. Add tests to test/math.test.js.
2. In src/strings.js add `slugify(text)` which lowercases, trims, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen and strips leading/trailing hyphens. Add tests to test/strings.test.js.
The two utilities touch different files and must be implemented as separate parallel tasks. `npm test` must pass with no regressions.

plan.summary: Add two independent named exports to the ESM library `acceptance-kit`: `clamp(value, min, max)` in src/math.js and `slugify(text)` in src/strings.js, each with unit tests appended to its existing node:test file. The two changes touch disjoint files (src/math.js + test/math.test.js vs. src/strings.js + test/strings.test.js) and are planned as two parallel worker tasks with no dependency between them. Verification is `npm test` (which runs `node --test`, per package.json line 6); the existing `add` and `capitalize` tests must keep passing.
assumptions: `clamp` only validates min > max (RangeError); no type validation of arguments is required since the request does not ask for it.
`slugify` treats 'alphanumeric' as ASCII a-z and 0-9 after lowercasing; non-ASCII letters (e.g. accented characters) count as non-alphanumeric and become hyphens. No transliteration is required.
`slugify` of an empty string or a string with no alphanumeric characters returns an empty string.
README.md does not need updating; the request only asks for code and tests.
No new dependencies or config: tests use the built-in node:test runner and node:assert/strict already used in test/math.test.js and test/strings.test.js.
The baseline `npm test` was not run by the planner (read-only role restricted to inspection commands); it is assumed to pass at HEAD 033dd4a.
acceptanceCriteria: src/math.js exports `clamp(value, min, max)` that returns value limited to the inclusive [min, max] range and throws a RangeError when min > max.
src/strings.js exports `slugify(text)` that lowercases, trims, replaces each run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, and strips leading/trailing hyphens.
test/math.test.js contains tests for `clamp` and test/strings.test.js contains tests for `slugify`.
`npm test` exits 0 with all tests passing, including the pre-existing `add` and `capitalize` tests, which remain unmodified.
Existing exports `add` and `capitalize` are unchanged, and no files other than the four src/test files are modified.

tasks.title: Add clamp(value, min, max) to src/math.js with tests
tasks.description:
Repository is an ESM JavaScript library (package.json has "type": "module"; test script is `node --test`). src/math.js currently contains a single named export `add(a, b)`, written without semicolons and with 2-space indentation. test/math.test.js imports `test` from 'node:test', `assert` from 'node:assert/strict', and `{ add }` from '../src/math.js', with one one-line test.

Do the following, touching ONLY src/math.js and test/math.test.js:
1. In src/math.js add a new named export `clamp(value, min, max)`. It must throw a `RangeError` when `min > max`; otherwise return `value` limited to the inclusive range [min, max] (min if value < min, max if value > max, else value). Leave `add` unchanged. Match the existing style (no semicolons, 2-space indent, `export function`).
2. In test/math.test.js extend the existing import to also import `clamp`, and add tests using the existing node:test + assert style covering: a value inside the range is returned unchanged; a value below min returns min; a value above max returns max; values equal to min and to max are returned as-is (inclusive bounds); min === max works; and `assert.throws(() => clamp(1, 5, 0), RangeError)` for min > max. Do not modify or remove the existing `add` test.
3. Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it exits 0.

Do not edit src/strings.js, test/strings.test.js, package.json, or README.md (another task is editing the strings files in parallel). Do not add dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: src/math.js exports a function `clamp` alongside the unchanged `add` export.
test/math.test.js contains clamp tests covering in-range, below-min, above-max, boundary values, and the RangeError case; the existing `add` test is intact.
Only src/math.js and test/math.test.js are modified by this task.

tasks.title: Add slugify(text) to src/strings.js with tests
tasks.description:
Repository is an ESM JavaScript library (package.json has "type": "module"; test script is `node --test`). src/strings.js currently contains a single named export `capitalize(text)`, written without semicolons and with 2-space indentation. test/strings.test.js imports `test` from 'node:test', `assert` from 'node:assert/strict', and `{ capitalize }` from '../src/strings.js', with one one-line test.

Do the following, touching ONLY src/strings.js and test/strings.test.js:
1. In src/strings.js add a new named export `slugify(text)`. It must lowercase the input, trim it, replace every run of one or more non-alphanumeric characters (anything other than a-z and 0-9 after lowercasing) with a single hyphen, and strip any leading and trailing hyphens. Leave `capitalize` unchanged. Match the existing style (no semicolons, 2-space indent, `export function`).
2. In test/strings.test.js extend the existing import to also import `slugify`, and add tests using the existing node:test + assert style covering: lowercasing and space replacement ('Hello World' -> 'hello-world'); surrounding whitespace trimmed ('  Hello World  ' -> 'hello-world'); a run of mixed non-alphanumerics collapses to one hyphen ('foo -- bar__baz' -> 'foo-bar-baz'); leading/trailing punctuation stripped ('--Hello, World!--' -> 'hello-world'); digits preserved ('Version 2 Release 10' -> 'version-2-release-10'); and input with no alphanumerics yields an empty string ('!!!' -> ''). Do not modify or remove the existing `capitalize` test.
3. Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it exits 0.

Do not edit src/math.js, test/math.test.js, package.json, or README.md (another task is editing the math files in parallel). Do not add dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: src/strings.js exports a function `slugify` alongside the unchanged `capitalize` export.
slugify('Hello World') === 'hello-world' and slugify('  Hello World  ') === 'hello-world'.
slugify('foo -- bar__baz') === 'foo-bar-baz' (runs collapse to a single hyphen).
slugify('--Hello, World!--') === 'hello-world' (no leading or trailing hyphens).
test/strings.test.js contains slugify tests covering lowercasing, trimming, run collapsing, leading/trailing hyphen stripping and digits; the existing `capitalize` test is intact.
Only src/strings.js and test/strings.test.js are modified by this task.

risks.description: A worker edits files belonging to the other parallel task (or shared files such as package.json), causing merge conflicts.
risks.mitigation: Each task description explicitly restricts edits to its own two files, and suggestedFiles are disjoint so the scheduler can run them in parallel safely.

risks.description: Ambiguity in slugify's definition of 'alphanumeric' (ASCII vs. Unicode letters) could lead to behaviour that differs from what the requester expects for non-ASCII input.
risks.mitigation: The ASCII-only interpretation is recorded as an assumption and stated in the task description; tests only pin ASCII behaviour that the request specifies.

risks.description: While both tasks run in parallel, `npm test` in one worktree may run before the other task's changes are merged, so a combined regression would only show after integration.
risks.mitigation: The files are fully independent (no shared imports between math and strings modules), and the mission-level criterion requires `npm test` to pass on the merged result.

risks.description: Existing tests could be accidentally altered when extending the import lines in the test files.
risks.mitigation: Task acceptance criteria require the existing `add` and `capitalize` tests to remain intact and passing.
